lxc_7b74260fd9a74941.text: When you lather soap on your hands, many soap molecules move toward the grease.

lxc_0fefb7a09f415907.text: Their oil-loving ends grab onto the grease.

lxc_bd7367372833fe43.text: At the same time, their water-loving ends point outward toward the water.

lxc_8b8a681a4ba65c68.text: The soap molecules form a tiny round group called a micelle.

lxc_040d38eccd2d20ab.text: The grease is trapped inside the micelle.

lxc_29dd12aeb2619b39.text: According to the American Chemical Society, these micelles let water carry the trapped grease away when you rinse.

lxc_9c776f99c1f33d11.text: You wash your hands every day.

lxc_e92a87d3ed4e2985.text: But how does soap actually remove grease and germs?

lxc_6fef7e82b7a859bb.text: Soap can do something water cannot do on its own: it connects water to oily dirt.

lxc_a435827c121c3554.text: Rubbing your hands together with soap is very important.

lxc_64c3267b428c760a.text: Rubbing helps the soap molecules reach all parts of your hands — between your fingers and under your nails.

lxc_04ea47500d3120a6.text: Lathering also helps lift germs and chemicals off the skin.

lxc_ada8baea2a2a6b5a.text: The CDC says that lather and rubbing help remove germs and chemicals, and that very hot water is not needed.

lxc_cace5fe0cd3e3bc2.text: Cool or warm water works well.

lxc_27481481641eaaab.text: A soap molecule is very small — too small to see.

lxc_46592811d977e366.text: But it has two ends that do different jobs.

lxc_c0a612f53ff8e290.text: The other end loves oil and fat.

lxc_36238b8e0e90f7e7.text: Because of this, soap can connect to both water and oil at the same time.

lxc_8bc550f867f76ca7.text: Think of soap as a tiny bridge between two things that do not usually mix.

lxc_addf49c79c056df8.text: The American Chemical Society explains that this is why soap works where water alone cannot.

lxc_169800666f9cc7b0.text: Water is very good at cleaning many things.

lxc_d402475808f2cff1.text: But water and oil do not mix.

lxc_89e9748e10fcba3f.text: When you pour oil into water, the oil floats on top.

lxc_9ac80eebdfd09011.text: It does not go into the water.

lxc_c69df6b2899310b8.text: This means if you rub greasy hands with only water, the grease stays on your skin.

lxc_9092b82a79a7f497.text: The water just moves around it.

lxc_52218bb6346e8e4a.text: According to the CDC, washing with only water is less effective than washing with soap.
